title: Why Loops Exist
summary: Discover why typing the same thing over and over is a problem — and how loops fix it.

content.title: The Copy-Paste Problem
content.summary: Repeating print() over and over is slow. There has to be a better way.
content.body:
Imagine you want a robot to shout "Jump!" five times. You could write this:

print("Jump!")
print("Jump!")
print("Jump!")
print("Jump!")
print("Jump!")

That works. But what if you want it 100 times? Or 1000? There has to be a better way.

content.title: Loops to the Rescue
content.summary: A for loop tells Python to repeat a block of code a set number of times.
content.body:
Python has a trick called a for loop. It lets you say "do this X times" in just two lines:

for i in range(5):
    print("Jump!")

That does the exact same thing as writing print("Jump!") five times — Python just handles the repetition for you.

content.title: What Does Each Part Mean?
content.summary: for starts the loop, range(5) controls how many times, and the indented line is what runs each time.
content.body:
for i in range(5):
    print("Jump!")

• for — starts the loop
• i — a counter variable Python updates automatically
• range(5) — tells Python to repeat 5 times
• The indented line — the code that runs each time

The indented block is called the loop body. Every time Python counts, it runs that block.

content.title: Indentation Is the Rule
content.summary: The loop body must be indented 4 spaces. Code outside the loop runs once after the loop finishes.
content.body:
The loop body must be indented — moved in by 4 spaces.

for i in range(3):
    print("Hello!")   <- runs 3 times

print("Done")        <- runs once, after the loop

If you forget the indent, Python shows an error.

editorPrompt: Make the robot shout your battle cry exactly 6 times using a for loop.
starterCode:
# Change this so it uses a loop instead of copy-paste!
print("Charge!")
print("Charge!")
print("Charge!")
progressiveHints: Start with: for i in range(6):
The next line needs to be indented (4 spaces), then write your print.
Replace the three print lines with just one inside the loop.
Answer: for i in range(6):\n    print("Charge!")
